name: Who Handles Curb, Gutter, and Apron Replacement?

mainEntity.name: Do driveway contractors in Los Angeles County handle curb, gutter, and apron replacement too?
mainEntity.text: Do driveway contractors in Los Angeles County handle curb, gutter, and apron replacement too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some driveway contractors do handle curb, gutter, and apron replacement, but that work is often a separate part of the project and may require additional coordination. The driveway apron is the transition area between the private driveway and the public street, so it can trigger different permit or inspection requirements from the main driveway slab. In Los Angeles County, the exact process depends on the city and whether the work affects sidewalk, curb, or gutter structures. Homeowners should ask whether the contractor will manage demolition, formwork, pour, finish, and any needed approvals for these areas. It is also important to confirm whether the quote includes restoration of nearby pavement, sidewalk, landscaping, or street striping if disturbed. A contractor who has handled local apron work before is more likely to anticipate these issues and avoid delays. If the scope is unclear, costs can increase once the job is underway.
acceptedAnswer.description: Many driveway contractors can handle curb, gutter, and apron work, but not every contractor includes it in their normal scope. These areas often involve different approvals, forms, and inspections because they connect to the public street. Homeowners should confirm whether the contractor is responsible for both the private driveway and the street-edge transition.
